name: Scapular Push-Up
description: The scapular push-up is a rehabilitation drill that trains serratus anterior strength and scapular protraction control in a push-up position. Unlike a standard push-up, the elbows remain locked throughout and only the shoulder blades move — protracting (spreading apart) and retracting (pinching together). It is prescribed for serratus anterior weakness, scapular winging, and shoulder instability.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a standard push-up position with arms fully extended, hands shoulder-width apart.
execution.setup_instructions: May also be performed from the knees for beginners, or against a wall for very early rehabilitation stages.
steps: Step 1: Assume a push-up position with arms straight and body in a rigid plank.
Step 2: Allow the shoulder blades to pinch together (retract), lowering the chest slightly between the arms without bending the elbows.
Step 3: Push the shoulder blades apart (protract), rounding the upper back slightly and reaching the hands into the floor.
Step 4: At full protraction, the upper back should be slightly rounded and the shoulder blades as far apart as possible.
Step 5: Return to the retracted position with control and repeat.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on protraction (spreading apart). Inhale on retraction.
common_mistakes: Bending the elbows — the elbows stay locked throughout
Moving the hips or lower back rather than isolating the shoulder blades
Not achieving full protraction at the top
safety_considerations: Appropriate for most populations including early post-operative shoulder patients when cleared by a clinician
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full retraction to full protraction. The range is typically 2–5 cm of vertical body travel.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2 seconds retract, 2 seconds protract. 15–20 reps × 2–3 sets.
coaching_cues: Arms stay completely straight — this is all shoulder blade
At the top, push the floor away and round the upper back like a cat
Feel the muscles around the shoulder blades working
